records.name: Karabük
records.summary: Inland Black Sea province, conservative province. No province-specific trans-related findings in this research pass; the national framework and its 2025-26 escalation apply here unchanged. The region's own sources are national-level: a leaked draft omnibus reform package (11th Judicial Package, October 2025) would create new anti-LGBT articles — criminalising conduct deemed "contrary to biological sex and general morality", restricting gender-affirming healthcare with a minimum age of 25, and enabling charges against trans people and their providers; the state's "Year of the Family" institutional programme and blanket bans on LGBTI public events are national practice, not provincial choices. Per the country research dossier, the absence of a documented provincial ban here is not evidence of tolerance — the national blanket-ban practice applies across the country.

records.name: Karaman
records.summary:
A trans visitor in Karaman is subject to the same nationwide developments as anywhere else in the country. An October 2025 leaked omnibus draft would amend the penal code to imprison acts deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality (up to three years; up to four for same-sex ceremonies), restrict gender-affirming healthcare to people 25 and over under infertility and repeated-evaluation conditions, and expose doctors to up to seven years in prison; national monitoring reports that 2025 hostility became explicit state policy — family-year directives from the head of state, a rights organisation closed, broadcast and arts-event censorship, three hate-motivated killings, 89 torture or ill-treatment violations and a 2.5-fold rise in detentions.

No statute, incident or court case specific to Karaman appears in the surviving sources for this record: the documents behind it are national-level and carry no provincial breakdown. The absence of province-specific documentation is not evidence of local tolerance — the nationwide framework and its 2025-26 escalation reach this province as any other.
